s1: This is a new ball, built on One Tree, One Ball.
A wound runs along one arm, with its middle at the centre of the ball.
Each cell is one step along that arm.
A chain of cells, held at both wound edges, solves exactly as cosh of n theta, over cosh of N theta.
So every gap junction is one peel step of the tree.
The beads show how much of the edge voltage reaches each cell.
s2: The shape of the wound decides how much reaches the middle.
At a half width of two decay lengths, a long cut keeps about twenty seven percent of the edge field.
A round wound in a sheet keeps forty four percent, and a round wound in a body keeps fifty five.
s3: The field travels with each edge, so it only has to reach the next row of cells, not the whole wound at once.
Measured skin wounds carry one hundred fifteen to one hundred eighty millivolts per millimeter at the edge, in a band about one millimeter wide.
s4: Gap junction coupling and membrane leak set the decay length.
Changing either one slides the wound edge across a fixed threshold shell.
The prediction, still untested, is that the widest wound keeping a chosen share at its middle grows as the square root of coupling over leak.
s5: Then the team checked the page.

On that physical map, the wall keeps one over root two of the edge field, at one point seven six decay lengths.

s6: One tree, one ball. Each cell a peel step, and the wound edge a shell.
